messages:
maya: Thinking aloud — we should run a dedicated simulation for mixed‑SKU spot pools that captures eviction correlation, AZ capacity skew, and realistic bin‑packing fragmentation. Current bench numbers don't reflect multi‑family diversity.

liam: +1. Are you thinking cross‑family (A100/H100/L4/G5) in the same pool or separate pools per family with routing?

maya: Prefer single logical pool surfaced to the scheduler but with multi‑instance‑type backing. Scheduler should prefer cheaper SKUs but avoid co‑placing too many same‑family instances in an AZ (eviction correlation risk). SLO: p95 infer latency < 220ms for 7B workload, < 20% fallback rate to dedicated lane.

serena: Two quick notes: fragmentation increases when instance types have different GPU counts/memory. Binpacking heuristics must be memory‑aware and prefer packing by sequence length buckets. Also need to track network egress limits per AZ — some regions throttle vNIC egress which spikes tail latency.

nate: Agreed. Proposed simulation inputs:
- instance types: a100-40g, h100-80g, g5-48g, l4-32g
- price curves: spot mean + std dev per AZ (empirical)
- eviction correlation matrix across instance types/azs
- workload mix: 60% 7B, 30% 2.7B quantized, 10% embeddings (cpu fallback)

nate: Sample ASG/mixed config snippet we can emulate in sim:

```yaml
fleet_policy:
  - instance_family: h100
    weight: 0.35
  - instance_family: a100
    weight: 0.4
  - instance_family: g5
    weight: 0.15
  - instance_family: l4
    weight: 0.1
fallback_lanes:
  - name: "degraded-7b"
    allowed_models: [redwood-7b-q4, redwood-7b-q4f]
    max_latency_inflation: 1.25
    priority: low
drain_policy:
  preempt_grace_secs: 45
  notify_hook: /ops/drain-hook.sh
```

ops-bot: evict-sim job queued: job-id=evict-sim-2026-09-14-77. We'll post results to #eng-infra when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

liam: One gotcha — AZ capacity: us-west1‑a has cheap h100 supply but often all h100s in that AZ are claimed simultaneously. If our weighting pushes too many h100s into us-west1, we see correlated mass evictions. Sim should model AZ affinity + cross‑AZ fallback cost (egress + latency).

serena: For fallback lanes: consider model slimming first (quantize/kv cache warmup) before moving to smaller models. Quantization reduces memory but can increase CPU decode cost; simulate token throughput delta. Quick numbers from last run: h100 spot avg $2.10/hr, a100 $1.25/hr, g5 $0.95/hr, l4 $0.30/hr. Effective cost/token shifts with Q4 quantization: ~35% lower cost but +5–10% p95 latency.

maya: Ok — acceptance criteria for sim:
- report eviction spikes (events/min) per AZ and per family
- p95 latency and fallback rate per workload bucket
- cost/token for each strategy (single‑pool mixed vs family‑segmented pools)
- sensitivity to correlation coef between instance families > 0.6

nate: I'll run an initial Monte Carlo with 10k trials using the above config. Command: 

```bash
./bin/eviction-sim --config sims/mixed-sku-2026.yaml --trials 10000 --out /tmp/evict-results.json
```

costbot: quick estimate (very rough) — baseline single‑family heavy weighting to h100 yields 18% lower nominal cost but 3x eviction spike frequency in worst AZ scenario. Mixed weighting reduces nominal savings to ~9% but lowers median eviction spike by ~60%.

liam: Nice. Action items: Nate to run sim and post results, Serena to prepare a fallback strategy decision tree (quantize -> cache -> model downgrade -> dedicated burst), Maya to prepare SLO thresholds to gate rollouts.

maya: Thanks — also log a follow up to test cross‑AZ warm standby (keep 2% reserved capacity in alternate AZs) and include egress penalty in the sim.

nate: Will do. Expect initial results in ~4h.

serena: If sim shows high correlation, we should consider explicit AZ diversity quotas in the fleet allocator (hard floor per AZ).

maya: Perfect. :+1:
